title: RuneScape built with Vibe Coding
author: Old_Swan8945
selftext:
If you were to build RuneScape again with 2026 technology (i.e., LLMs, modern game engines like UE5, marketplace, ad assets, etc.), what would you keep the same and what would you change? 

Much of the RuneScape graphics and game design were built around the technology limits of the time but yet it's still one of the enduring games 20+ years later. 

Would you try to build it with the photo real aesthetic? I'm not sure I actually would. I think I might actually just build it with low-poly assets and try to focus on the gameplay loop as much as possible. 

That being said it should be possible to build so much more content into the game but I'm not sure the focus should be on graphics. 

What do people think?

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: Definitely not photo realistic. I'd stay low poly. WAY faster iteration and WAY faster to get it to look good. The #1 thing I'd do is find a pipeline to get from assets to game-ready animations.

comments.author: cant-game-anymore
comments.body: Quite frankly I think nobody should try to rebuild RuneScape. It’s there and it’s still good. If you gonna build something, build something new.

replies.author: USDJPYFX
replies.body: 100% competing against the beast that osrs is a big task. They dominate that specific genre.

replies.author: Old_Swan8945
replies.body: The question didn’t specify that I or anyone was going to compete against OSRS. Just asked how you would build a game like it using modern tech.

replies.author: Old_Swan8945
replies.body:
Don't see how this is a helpful answer and don’t understand why this is getting upvoted. I didn’t ask whether rebuilding RuneScape was a project worth doing or an opinion on whether it should be done. 

I asked how you would do it, supposing you had decided to, and you didn’t answer that question.

comments.author: kilographix
comments.body: The focus would be on thr gsme loop but Runescape has epic storylines and quests with a lot of easter eggs that make it as good as it is. Any AI replica would almost definitely feel more AI and be less enjoyable.

comments.author: Zachieepoo
comments.body: I have been working on my own take of RuneScape. Been busy vibe coding it. Low poly graphics, less skills but more interactive, but hopefully not more tedious. My take on it. Elements of EverQuest and WOW mixed in.

replies.author: Old_Swan8945
replies.body: Would love to give it a try whenever you are ready to share or just see early concept art or specs. There's been good discussion on the discord as well on this concept. I'm not sure if you're there as well.

replies.author: Zachieepoo
replies.body: I didn't know about a discord. DM me the link.

replies.author: Party-Doughnut-4051
replies.body: I'm also interested in this and would love to take a look!

replies.author: Zachieepoo
replies.body: I'll do a post soon about it with some screenshots.

comments.author: Necessary-Warthog-63
comments.body: You see this is what is wrong with most people that use ai. They think "hey let's just make this thing that already exists..." its stupid and a waste. Make something new. Stop trying to make ai clones of everything. Or do you really want the 50th post of I vibe coded another mmo or I built another trading card game.

replies.author: Old_Swan8945
replies.body:
I actually appreciate the posts where people show the clones they built. I think it helps demonstrate the art of the possible and enhance our collective understanding. 

I’d actually say that this post is what’s wrong with many people who use Reddit. They take an honest question and use it as an opportunity to flex their superior knowledge. 

Wheres your ai clone? What work have you made? Would love to see it. Genuinely.

comments.author: Final_Homework_9491
comments.body:
Music was key. Rarity of gear was key. I loved way you could pick up items from ground. Original wilderness was key. Progression of tasks was key, like having higher level ores or trees

Imagine RuneScape but every time a player walks far enough it autogenerates new terrain and city like Minecraft

replies.author: Old_Swan8945
replies.body:
Yeah and then how do you make it consistent across multiple players? That would be really hard if it’s an infinite world.

And what if you could build the cities rather than just live in one the devs made?

replies.author: Final_Homework_9491
replies.body:
Just make map generate in chunks like Minecraft - if it’s doable in Minecraft it’s doable in any game

Building cities would be interesting, I like that idea
